title: Triple-product expectation as a subset average
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\delta\in[0,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be odd, so that $f(-x)=-f(x)$. Choose independently at each coordinate a sign triple by selecting $(U,V,-V)$ with probability $\delta$ and $(U,V,-UV)$ otherwise, with independent uniform signs $U,V$. The expectation of the product of $f$ on the three query vectors is $\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\widehat f(S)^2 A_{\delta,f}(S)$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $A_{\delta,f}(S)$ is the average over subsets $K$ with weight $(1-\delta)^{|K|}\delta^{n-|K|}$ of $(-1)^{|S\cap K|}\widehat f(S\cap K)$.
